newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Bhutto activists detained, Pakistan stocks surge.
newsitem.headline: Bhutto activists detained, Pakistan stocks surge.

text.p: Pakistani police on Wednesday detained about two dozen demonstrators protesting against the sacking of prime minister Benazir Bhutto, who remained confined by police to her home one day after being abruptly dismissed.

Activists from Bhutto's Pakistan People's Party (PPP) burned an effigy of President Farooq Leghari, who dismissed the National Assembly and named octogenarian Meraj Khalid as interim prime minister to supervise elections set for February 3.

Witnesses said police and PPP workers threw stones at each other outside the party's headquarters in the capital Islamabad. Police entered the building and arrested about 10 party workers, PPP officials and witnesses said.
In a separate incident earlier on Thursday, police detained 10 activists from a score of PPP supporters who protested on Wednesday along the main Jinnah Avenue in the capital.
"O God, O Prophet, Benazir is innocent," demonstrators shouted. There were no reports of injuries.

Bhutto, sacked for the second time in her turbulent political career, remained a virtual prisoner in her official Islamabad residence, but had been allowed to meet colleagues and take telephone calls, a government official said.

Lawyers for the caretaker government told a court on Wednesday that Bhutto was not under arrest, saying she was under police protection for her personal safety. Phone lines to her residence, which were cut on Tuesday, remained disconnected.
Bhutto aides said she hoped to hold a news conference later on Wednesday.

Lawyers for the caretaker government asked the court in Rawalpindi, near Islamabad, to reject a habeas corpus petition filed on Tuesday by lawyers for former defence minister Aftab Shaaban Meerani, pleading that Bhutto had been "held unlawfully incommunicado".
"It is vehemently denied that the former Prime Minister is under arrest," they said. "(A) Police contingent is deployed for (the) personal safety of the former prime minister."

A government official said Bhutto's husband, Asif Ali Zardari, had been flown to Rawalpindi late on Tuesday from Lahore, where he had been detained soon after Leghari dismissed Bhutto's government in the early hours of Tuesday.
On the Karachi Stock Exchange share prices ended 5.25 percent higher as Bhutto's dismissal raised hopes of a serious anti-corruption drive under the new caretaker government, brokers said.
In its biggest rise this year, the Karachi stock exchange's 100-share index jumped 78.63 points to end at 1,577.40.
Brokers said the market was enthused by expectations of an end to a long period of political and economic uncertainty under Bhutto.
"People are bullish since the government was removed yesterday," one broker said.
Khalid and his nine ministers held their first cabinet meeting on Wednesday morning. A spokesman was expected to brief reporters later in the day.

In a sign of continued fallout from the federal shakeup, Leghari replaced two provincial governors, one from Punjab, the other from North West Frontier Province, with high court chief justices, a presidential spokesman said.
The caretaker government sacked many senior bureaucrats linked to Bhutto, including top economic advisers V.A. Jafarey and Shahid Hasan Khan.
